T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Tariff risks, US-China summit, Fed rate path uncertainty
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Tech investment cycle durability, China trade surplus trajectory, domestic demand structural weakness

**Synopsis:**
China's August 2026 trade data showed exports surging 25% YoY and imports +28.2% YoY, driven by AI/tech products, EVs, and semiconductors. The trade surplus widened to $119.09B, on pace to top $1 trillion annually for the second consecutive year. Domestic demand remains structurally weak, with growth having cooled to 4.3% in Q2. A US-China trade truce is holding, with reciprocal tariff cuts under negotiation ahead of a presidential summit. Chinese analysts see no imminent case for PBoC rate cuts given resilient external demand. Markets were largely unmoved, awaiting US CPI data.
